Hannah / Karthik — I reviewed Novafin's redlines and drafted a response. High-level legal guidance and suggested language below. (See attached: Redwood_MSA_response_20250813.docx for a full redline.)

Concise legal positions
- Auto-renew: We should stick to a 60-day prior notice for opt-out. Operationally, renewals are batched and require lead time; 30 days is high risk. If they insist on 30 days, require notice by registered email and make renewal effective on the later of the date in the Order Form or 30 days after notice.
- Termination for convenience: We can accept mutual termination for convenience with 30 days' notice, but propose mutuality (both parties) and carve out an exception for outstanding SOWs or active pilots.
- Uncancellable period: Instead of fully removing it, convert the uncancellable window into a pricing commitment — i.e., customer receives preferential pricing for the first 90 days but can terminate with a termination fee if they exit earlier. This preserves predictability and is easier to operationalize.

Proposed sample language (brief):
"
- Auto-Renew: The Initial Term shall automatically renew for successive Renewal Terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current Term.
- Termination for Convenience: Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other party, provided that termination shall not relieve Customer of payment obligations for Services already rendered and any termination fee set forth in the Order Form.
- Uncancellable Commitment: Customer shall be eligible for the discounted pricing set forth in the Order Form during the first ninety (90) days of the Initial Term; early termination by Customer within such period shall trigger a termination fee equal to twenty percent (20%) of remaining committed fees, as set forth in the Order Form.
"

Risks and negotiation levers
- The termination fee will be the main leverage to preserve value if they want unconstrained convenience termination.
- If Novafin pushes on 30-day auto-renew notice, we should ask for a trade (e.g., longer notice for changes to price, or a minimum spend commitment).

I'll attach the redline and a clean copy. Once we agree on wording, Hannah can send to Marta.

Hi Marta / Alex — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. We reviewed with legal and commercial and can propose the following compromise set of edits (attached as "Redwood_MSA_response_20250813.docx"):

1) Auto-Renew: Redwood to retain a sixty (60) day prior written notice requirement to opt-out of renewal. We recognize Novafin's operational needs — to make this more customer-friendly we offer a calendar-based alert 75 days prior to renewal and a single-point-of-contact to manage notices.

2) Termination for Convenience: Redwood is willing to accept mutual termination for convenience on thirty (30) days’ notice. To balance commercial commitments, early termination within the first 90 days will trigger a termination fee equal to 20% of remaining committed fees (specified in the Order Form).

3) Uncancellable/Commitment Period: Instead of removing the commitment period entirely, the discounts in the Order Form will be conditioned on a 90-day pricing commitment. If Novafin needs fully cancellable services from day one, we can offer that at a higher (list) rate.

Next steps

- If you prefer alternate language, send redlines back and we will aim to respond within 48 hours.
